transcript: Solution engineer: What is the pain?
Plant manager: We lose more time on changeovers than on breakdowns and we cannot say exactly where. Four packing lines, each changes over three or four times a day.
Production supervisor: Three lines. Line four has been down since spring.
Plant manager: Three running, four installed. Fine.
Continuous improvement lead: We do manual time studies twice a year. They are out of date the week after.
Solution engineer: What signals exist on the lines?
Controls engineer: Each line has a PLC with run, stop and fault states, and the reason codes operators enter. The codes are mostly "other".
Solution engineer: Can the PLC states be read without touching the line?
Controls engineer: Yes, through the historian. Read-only OPC access is already set up for the energy dashboard.
Production supervisor: The operators will not enter better codes just because you ask. They are busy.
Solution engineer: So what would help?
Continuous improvement lead: Seeing the changeover as steps, with the gap between the last good pack and the first good pack after it, per line, per shift.
Plant manager: And a weekly view I can put in front of the shift leads.
Solution engineer: Is there a camera on the lines?
Production supervisor: One per line, for quality disputes. Not great angles.
Controls engineer: I would rather not depend on the cameras. The PLC data is enough to start.
Solution engineer: Agreed for a first phase. What is the baseline?
Continuous improvement lead: The last time study said forty minutes average changeover on line two. I do not trust it for the others.
Plant manager: Use it anyway. It is what the board has seen.
Continuous improvement lead: I would rather we measured for two weeks first.
Solution engineer: Who owns changeover time as a number?
Plant manager: Me, ultimately. The supervisors own it per shift.
Solution engineer: Any constraints on data or access?
Controls engineer: Nothing writes to the PLCs. Historian access is read-only and stays that way. Data can go to our cloud tenant, IT already approved that for the energy work.
Production supervisor: Operators must be told what it is. Last time someone put a screen up without saying why and it went badly.
Solution engineer: Noted. Anything else you discussed that we should park?
Plant manager: Predicting breakdowns. Everyone wants it, nobody has the data for it.

traps.note: Four packing lines (L2) versus three, line four is down (L3).
Use the old time study as baseline (L19) versus measure for two weeks first (L20).
The baseline is disputed and must stay open.

follow_up.real_answer: Agreed with the plant manager: measure all three running lines for two weeks before go-live and use that as the baseline, with the CI lead owning the number.
follow_up.non_answer: TBC, the plant manager and the CI lead still disagree.
